stem: The graphs of $f(x)={=b}^{x}$ and $g(x)=-{=a}x^{2}+q$ are drawn on the same system of axes. Both graphs pass through the point $A$ on the $y$-axis. The point $B$ lies on the graph of $f$ and the point $C$ lies on the graph of $g$; both points have $x$-coordinate ${=m}$. Calculate the length of $BC$.
solution: $f(0)={=b}^{0}=1$, so $A=(0, 1)$. (Every graph of the form $y=b^{x}$ passes through $(0, 1)$.)
$B$ and $C$ have the same $x$-coordinate, so $BC$ is vertical and $BC={=fb}-({=gm})={=fb - gm}$.
notes: Advanced: the book's own twist from Ex 6.8 Q50 (f(x) = 4^x and g(x) = -4x^2 + q meeting at A(0, 1), with B on f and C on g above the same x). The only exponential-graph fact needed is the common y-intercept (0, 1), which fixes q; g is then only evaluated, never analysed, so no quadratic-graph technique beyond substitution is used. The stem is written out in words, so the book's figure is not needed (it was read: it shows f, g, A on the y-axis, B on f, C on g, with BC vertical and dashed). b and a are drawn from 2..5 (a >= 2 avoids a printed coefficient of 1) and m from 1..2, giving 32 distinct stems with answers 5 to 44. g(m) = 1 - a m^2 is always negative, so C is always below B and the subtraction is always B minus C with brackets. Reviewers: if quadratics are judged out of scope for this objective, drop this family; the other two stand without it.
